title: SBA stage result
description: The structured result of one stage of one run, one entry per host. Written to result.<stage>.json in the run-state store and delivered as an artifact rather than scraped from a log (AD-14). This document exists because a failure that is only a log line is a failure nobody can act on: the per-host status says which server, the error says which code and whether a retry is worthwhile, and the remediation block gives the operator a command that is safe to run. A requester told only FAILED files a ticket; a requester told which stage failed and given the command fixes it themselves. See AD-01, AD-14, AD-16, and docs/api/api-contract.md section 1.5.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this schema. See AD-20.

request_id.description: The originating request. The join key to the run state and, downstream, to the request record. See AD-04 and AD-05.

correlation_id.description: Propagated from the run context into every log line, so a support request quoting one string finds the whole run. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 4.3.

run_id.description: This execution attempt. Distinct from request_id so that a resumed run is distinguishable from the original in the state store. See docs/architecture/idempotency.md section 5.

stage.description: The stage this result describes. The closed set is what makes the stage table statically enumerable, and it is the same set the run context accepts for lifecycle.stage -- two divergent lists would mean a stage could be dispatched that could not be reported. See AD-01 and docs/architecture/role-dependency-model.md.

attempt.description: 1-based attempt number. Present because a stage result from attempt 2 and one from attempt 3 are different evidence, and folding them into a single latest-value would lose the record that a retry happened. See docs/architecture/failure-and-retry.md.

status.description: The stage outcome, rolled up from the per-host statuses. SUCCESS means every host completed. PARTIAL is a first-class terminal state that is also resumable: terminal for the automation, because nothing further happens automatically, and resumable for a human, because re-running the stage continues from where it stopped. Mapping PARTIAL to a single boolean loses that distinction, and it is the most likely implementation mistake in a status model. MANUAL_ATTENTION is not terminal in the same sense -- it means the run is waiting for a person. See docs/architecture/request-lifecycle.md section 2 and docs/api/api-contract.md section 2.

started_at.description: When the stage began, RFC 3339 UTC. Wall-clock stamps are added by the caller, never read by the resolver, which is what keeps the resolver pure. See AD-22.

finished_at.description: When the stage ended, RFC 3339 UTC. Equal to started_at for a stage that was skipped, which is how a skip is distinguished from a stage that never ran.

duration_s.description: Elapsed seconds. Bounded at 86400 because a stage that reports a longer duration than a day is a clock problem, and an unbounded number here would corrupt every duration roll-up on the result.

execution_engine.description: The engine that executed the stage. Transport metadata, recorded so an operator knows where to look -- but never branched on by a consumer, because engine dispatch is an implementation detail and a consumer that branches on it has coupled itself to one. See AD-09, AD-21, and docs/api/api-contract.md section 4.5.

execution_url.description: Link to the engine run, so an operator can reach the raw job. Recorded for correlation only; it is never a required field, because a result that cannot be produced without a URL would fail in a context that has no browser to open it.

code.description: What produced this result. Three values that together make a run reproducible and auditable: the code, the image, and the configuration. A run that can be reproduced from its own result is one that can be debugged after the fact.

sba_git_sha.description: The full 40-character commit the run executed. Full rather than short because a seven-character abbreviation is ambiguous across the history of a busy repository, and an ambiguous provenance record is worse than none. See docs/architecture/cicd-pipeline.md.

sba_ee_digest.description: The immutable digest of the execution environment, not its tag. The same digest must run nonprod and prod, or a production build can behave differently from the one that was tested -- which is the failure the whole promotion model exists to prevent. See docs/architecture/execution-environment.md.

catalog_version.description: The configuration tree version, carried from the run context. See docs/architecture/configuration-resolution.md section 5.

hosts.description: One entry per host the stage addressed, in creation order. Every host is present whether it succeeded, failed, or was skipped, because a host that is absent from the list is indistinguishable from a host that was forgotten -- and an omitted host is exactly the one an operator needs to know about. See docs/architecture/request-lifecycle.md.

sba_instance_id.description: The golden join key, correlating this entry with the run context, the GCP label, the DNS record and the CMDB CI. See AD-05.

short_name.description: NetBIOS name of the host, at most 15 characters. Carried on every stage result so an operator reading a failure never has to join against the context to learn which server it was. See AD-06.

fqdn.description: Fully qualified name. Present from the validate stage onward, where it is derived, so that a DNS or CMDB failure can be read without a lookup. See AD-06.

status.description: This host's outcome. The same vocabulary as the stage status, which is what makes the roll-up rule expressible as a table over (stage, host) pairs and testable rather than described. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 10.

changed.description: Whether this host was modified. The idempotence assertion: a re-run of a completed stage must report changed == false. A stage that reports changed on a no-op re-run has a non-idempotent task, and this field is how CI catches it. See docs/architecture/idempotency.md section 3.

duration_s.description: Elapsed seconds for this host. Per host as well as per stage because a PARTIAL stage is usually one slow host and one fast one, and the total alone cannot tell an operator which.

gcp.description: The GCP state of this host, as read back. Read-only observation, and the substrate of assert_instance: a stage assertion that does not actually re-read live state is worse than none, because it converts an unverified assumption into a recorded success. See docs/architecture/provider-abstraction.md section 3.4.

zone.description: Zone holding the instance. Immutable after creation, so a read-back that disagrees with the context is IMMUTABLE_MISMATCH and never a converge target. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 4.

machine_type.description: Fully qualified machine type as read back, so a resize is verified rather than assumed to have taken effect. See docs/architecture/provider-abstraction.md section 3.2.

self_link.description: The instance self link. The provider-specific resource identifier recorded on the result and the CI, and the value a destroy keys on. See docs/architecture/provider-abstraction.md section 2.

private_ip.description: The internal address. The only address the platform records, since placement.external_ip is always false. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 6.

labels_converged.description: Whether the GCP labels already matched the resolved metadata, verified by a read-back. This is invariant I-6 of AD-11 and the reason the overwhelming majority of re-runs produce no control-plane events at all. When false, reboot_required is true: labels can only be set at creation on GCP, so a correction is a stop, modify, start -- which is a reboot-equivalent event and is reported as one rather than hidden inside a changed count. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md sections 3.2 and 3.4.

reboot_required.description: Whether a reboot-equivalent stop/start is required to reach the desired state, which on GCP is the only way to change a label. Explicit rather than implied by changed, because a reboot is a disruptive event for a production host and must be visible in the result rather than discovered from a dropped session. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 3.4.

adopted.description: Whether the instance already existed and was adopted rather than created. Recorded because it is the difference between a build and a recovery, and a destroy is only ever permitted to delete resources where adopted is false -- deleting an adopted resource would destroy something the platform did not create. See docs/architecture/provider-abstraction.md section 3.1 and docs/architecture/idempotency.md section 10.

image.description: The image self link as read back, compared against the pinned value. A mismatch is OS_VERSION_MISMATCH and is not retryable: the remedy is a rebuild, not a retry. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 5.

error.description: Why this host failed. Present exactly when status is not SUCCESS, so that a SUCCESS entry carrying an error is rejected by the resolver's own consistency check rather than being quietly ignored downstream.

diagnostics.description: Structured findings that are not failures. Warnings, degraded conditions, and assertions that passed marginally. Present so a stage can report something an operator needs without inventing a failure to carry it -- a warning promoted to an error trains people to ignore warnings, and a warning dropped entirely means the condition is never noticed.

level.description: Severity. A closed set, so a consumer switches on it rather than parsing the message.

code.description: An identifier from the error registry, so a diagnostic is queryable by the same vocabulary as a failure. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 3.2.

message.description: A message from the closed template set. Never a raw exception, never a secret, and never a configuration value that could be sensitive, because this text reaches a requester-facing surface. A sanitisation test in CI is what keeps that promise honest. See docs/api/api-contract.md sections 3.1 and 10.

host_short_name.description: The host this concerns, when it concerns one. Absent for a run-wide finding.

remediation.description: What the operator should do next. This is the block that turns a failure into a resolution, and it is the reason stage independence (AD-01) and retention (AD-16) are worth their cost: because nothing is destroyed and any stage can be re-run alone, there is always a next action that is safe. A PARTIAL without this block is a ticket; a PARTIAL with it is a fix.

recommand.description: A ready-to-run command. Extra-vars here contain only a path to the stored context and the stage name -- never a value from it -- because extra-vars are logged by the engine and anything placed there is disclosed. See AD-15 and docs/security/secret-management.md.

note.description: What the command will and will not do, in one sentence. Stating that re-running will not re-provision is the single most useful sentence in the document, because the natural fear after a failed build is that a retry will create a duplicate server.

reversible.description: Whether the stage is safely re-runnable. False only where re-running would itself be destructive, which in this release is nowhere: every stage is idempotent, and a stage that is not is a bug rather than a case. Present so a future stage can declare itself irreversible without inventing a new field.

host_error.description: A single host's failure. The code is a stable machine-readable identifier, never localised and never reworded, because consumers switch on it; the message is built from a closed template set and is what a human reads; and retryable is a property of the condition rather than of the stage, which is the distinction most easily got wrong. DOMAIN_DC_UNREACHABLE is retryable and DOMAIN_CREDENTIAL_INVALID is not, and they are the same stage -- classifying by stage would get this wrong, and retrying a credential failure would multiply failed logons and could lock the service account. See docs/api/api-contract.md sections 3.1 and 3.2, and docs/architecture/failure-and-retry.md section 4.2.

code.description: The error code. A code is never renamed or repurposed; a retired code becomes RESERVED, so a consumer that switches on it keeps working. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 3.2.

retryable.description: Whether an automatic retry is worthwhile. A quota or an IP exhaustion is not retryable because it does not restore itself inside a retry window, so retrying is pure delay; a rate limit is retryable and the two are routinely confused. See docs/architecture/failure-and-retry.md section 2.

message.description: What happened, from a closed template set. Never a raw exception and never a secret. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 3.1.

actionable.description: What to do instead. The field that prevents a ticket. Optional on a per-host stage error because the stage-level remediation covers it, and required on the requester-facing result. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 3.1.

detail_source.description: A JSON pointer into the stored context, e.g. context.json#/preflight/13. The detail is referenced rather than inlined so that the response stays small and does not leak estate topology into a widely-readable surface. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 3.1 and section 5.3.

stage_detail.description: The task or role that failed, e.g. system.domain_join. Present because a stage name alone points at a stage of eight tasks, and this is what narrows it to one.

error_code.description: The stable error registry, enumerated so that a code cannot be invented at a call site and so that CI can assert every code a role can raise is a code the registry documents. Codes are contract: a consumer may switch on them. See docs/api/api-contract.md section 3.2.
